processList.title: Apps
processList.emptyHint: Play sound in an app, then refresh
processList.stopRoute: Stop output and return to the system default
processList.stopAllConfirm: Click again to return everything to the system default
processList.multiSelectHint: Click to select; Ctrl+click to pick several and send them together

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device, in percent
deviceVolume.hint: Attenuates this device relative to the loudest one in its group. Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}}% a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value
deviceVolume.inactive: Not applied right now: volume balancing only runs in multi-device duplication routes
deviceVolume.primary: The system plays this device directly, so software cannot attenuate it; its value anchors the group's loudest level

deviceDelay.hint: Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}} a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value
deviceDelay.inactive: Not applied right now: delay compensation only runs in multi-device duplication routes; a single-device route is played by the system directly
deviceDelay.primary: The system plays this device directly (the route's anchor); its value only shifts the alignment reference of the whole group

sourceLevel.valueLabel: Level this app gives the audio of {{process}}, in percent
sourceLevel.hint: Level this app gives this program's audio on its way to the devices it is duplicated to, as a percentage: 100 leaves it as the program produced it, below attenuates, above amplifies. Like the device volume and the delay, it acts on the mirrored copies — the device Windows plays directly is not affected by it. Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}}% a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value

deviceLatency.hint: Software-side latency only: the engine's pipeline for this device plus the endpoint's own reported stream latency. What a codec or a Bluetooth link adds on top is invisible to the app, so what you hear is later than this
deviceLatency.unmeasured: Not measured: this device is being duplicated, but its endpoint has not reported a latency for the stream — nothing has been assumed in its place
deviceLatency.inactive: Nothing to measure: no engine is duplicating this device — a single-device route is played by the system directly
deviceLatency.primary: Not measurable: the system plays this device directly (the route's anchor), so there is no stream of ours to ask

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each process's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.advancedModeDesc: Show per-device delay and volume readouts plus the full activity log
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Releases a program that no longer follows the system's playback device; routed programs are left alone
settings.stopAllRoutesDesc: Returns every routed program to the system default at once. The programs a route is not using are left alone.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: Close hides the window to the tray while routes keep running; turned off, closing quits and stops them
settings.autostartDesc: Launches silently into the tray at sign-in; remembered routes are ready before you open anything
settings.delayNote: Drag or scroll the number under a device node on the main screen. Applies in multi-device routes only — a single-device route is played by the system directly.
settings.calibrationNote: The measured latency covers the software side only; what a Bluetooth link itself adds cannot be measured here, so align by ear.
settings.delayRangeDesc: Delays can be set within this ± range
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.sourceLevelsAlignDesc: Brings every duplicating program that is playing up to the loudest one's level
settings.sourceLevelsNote: A level is the gain applied to this app's own copy of a program's audio; the program's own volume and anything Windows stores are untouched. 100 leaves it as produced, and it acts on the mirrored copies only.
settings.sourceLevelsNone: No program is being duplicated right now; a level applies in multi-device routes only.
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust talking to Windows Core Audio directly, no third-party executables.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — let it play a sound and try again.
startup.firstRunBody: Select an app on the left, pick a device, then confirm at the center button — output moves there. Pick several devices to output to all of them at once. If a program ever stops following the device you switch to in Windows, the per-app output reset in Settings releases it.
